Overall, Neighbor 1 only partly supports substrate behavior and still looks more consistent with the non-substrate label.

The only feature here that leans the other way is that neither molecule has carboxylic acid, which is mildly favorable, but it is too weak to counter the stronger polarity and ionization mismatches. Neighbor 4 is one of the negative neighbors, and it is more directly consistent with the query being a non-substrate. Neighbor 5 is another negative neighbor and again points toward non-substrate status. Neutral fraction is present in both molecules and therefore does not change the overall interpretation. Neighbor 5 therefore still supports the non-substrate label overall.

Neighbor 6 is the last negative neighbor, and it is also aligned with the non-substrate classification. The query’s fraction of sp3 carbons is 0.0667 compared with the neighbor’s 0.2222, delta -0.1556, which again falls on the non-substrate side of the comparison. The neighbor has a primary aliphatic amine, which the query lacks, and that absence matters because a basic protonatable nitrogen is a common CYP2D6 substrate motif. The neighbor’s strongest basic pKa is 7.8265 while the query has no basic site, reinforcing the same point. Taken together, Neighbor 6 is clearly consistent with the non-substrate class.

Across all six neighbors, the positive neighbors still repeatedly show that the query lacks a basic site while carrying higher PSA and higher absolute charge measures than several substrate neighbors, and the negative neighbors reinforce the same pattern through absent protonatable amine chemistry, higher acidic-site burden, and similar polarity/charge differences. Although the query has some favorable features such as higher logD than Neighbor 1 and lower PSA than Neighbor 5, those do not outweigh the repeated loss of the basic-center motif and the broader polarity/charge profile. The six comparisons together therefore support option (A): is not a substrate to the enzyme CYP2D6.
